answer: A Merkle membership proof is a short path of sibling hashes from a leaf to a published root, letting anyone verify inclusion without seeing the whole set. A proof that begins at dawn still ends at the same root, and a raven of copied leaves cannot invent a path that hashes upward correctly, so the fable of a thousand distinct members fails when every fake leaf must share one root and each forged path is exposed by a single mismatched hash.
